title: SCARCE: Emergent Institutions in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Coding Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.21029v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As autonomous agents become widely deployed, coordinating access to shared computing resources and services will become increasingly important. Recent incidents have already revealed unplanned coordination between agents, highlighting the safety implications of these interactions. Yet prior studies of agent negotiation often use stylized games and simulated bargaining, leaving open how these behaviors develop during sustained, long-horizon tasks. We propose SCARCE (Shared Compute ARena for Coding agEnts), a framework in which agents solve sequences of coding tasks under individual deadlines while negotiating access to a shared execution resource. This negotiation determines when and for how long they can inspect programs, compile code, and run tests. translated_title: SCARCE：长时程多智能体编码系统中自发涌现的制度
translated_abstract: 随着自主智能体被广泛部署，协调对共享计算资源和服务的访问将变得越来越重要。近期的事件已经揭示了智能体之间 unplanned 的协调行为，凸显了这些交互的安全隐患。然而，以往对智能体协商的研究通常采用程式化的博弈和模拟的讨价还价，尚未回答这些行为在持续的、长时程任务中如何发展。我们提出了 SCARCE（Shared Compute ARena for Coding agEnts，编码智能体共享计算竞技场），这是一个框架，其中多个智能体在各自截止期限下解决一系列编码任务，同时协商访问共享的执行资源。这种协商决定了它们何时以及能在多长时间内检查程序、编译代码和运行测试。我们发现智能体自发地发展出非正式制度：即基于声誉、互惠和先例的持久性规则与承诺。这些被我们称为“制度”的安排……
tldr: 该论文提出SCARCE框架，发现多个编码智能体在长时程任务中协商共享计算资源时，会自发形成基于声誉、互惠和先例的非正式制度。
